message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 180, "amount_cents": 13791}, {"order_id": 181, "amount_cents": 1851}, {"order_id": 184, "amount_cents": 3930}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds, so I'll start by listing refunds.

The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly (orders 180, 181, 184 with the same amounts), so I can proceed. I need the customer list before I can get net balances, so I'll call list_orders.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report, and the orders show three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
The refunds match Alpha's report, and acme's net of 13345 is consistent with order 180 (16857) minus its 13791 refund plus order 183 (10279). I'll record acme's payout.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll get birch's net balance from net_balance rather than computing it myself.
Birch's net of 35150 matches the orders (26275 + 14656) minus refunds (1851 + 3930), so I'll record birch's payout.
Acme and birch are paid. The only customer left is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance.
Cobalt's net of 31469 matches its orders (26600 + 4869) with no refunds against it, so I'll record its payout.
All three customers have been paid. Each payout matches its order and refund arithmetic, and the orders list contains no other customers. Finishing with the payouts I recorded.
